text:
michelle: Quick question — UX/contract for saved quickfilters. When a user saves a view on a route that includes a model-scoped filter, which scope should be authoritative on load: the route's persisted filter or the model's default filter? I ran into conflicting state in the prototype.
jason: My gut: preserve the exact saved view the user created (route-scoped). If the model changes its defaults later we can show a hint but don't mutate user's saved query.
anita: +1 for not mutating. But we need a clear precedence rule. Proposal: explicit saved query state wins. If route + model present, treat saved query as a bundle with metadata "source_scope":"route" or "model" so we can explain in UI.
michelle: That works. Two follow-ups: 1) how do we show telemetry when model defaults change vs user overrides? 2) what about quota & routing hints embedded in saved queries (e.g., prefer-dedicated: true)?
devon: For telemetry, we should tag samples with the effective scope used at runtime: e.g., `effective_scope=route` or `effective_scope=model_default`. That way evals/alerts can attribute regressions to scope drift.
leo: On quotas/routing hints — those feel operational. Saved views should be purely observational (filters, sort). If we allow `routing_hint` in saved queries we need a clear permission check and audit trail. Otherwise teams will accidentally change inference behavior by sharing queries.
emily: I sketched a minimal saved-query JSON we could store on the console backend (won't mutate existing API):
```
{
  "name": "High-cost-models",
  "scope": "route",        // route | model | org
  "filters": [{"field":"model","op":"eq","value":"redwood/omega-v1"}],
  "meta": {"created_by":"michelle","created_at":"2026-03-19T15:22:00Z","source_scope":"route"}
}
```
emily: Note: `meta.source_scope` is important for rollout UI to call out why a filter is present.
jason: UX idea: when opening a saved view, show a small pill: "applied from: route" with a chevron that expands to show "model defaults" and allow a one-click apply-to-route (copy as route-saved) so users can adopt model changes intentionally.
anita: Implementation note: backend should store a `derived_from` pointer for model-scoped saves. That makes it easier to surface diffs when the model's default filter changes.
michelle: How do we handle telemetry sampling? Some routes have high qps so saved-views usage telemetry will skew. Can we sample or attribute by user action?
devon: We already have per-route sampling flags. Proposal: record an event `saved_view.open` with attributes `{route, saved_view_id, effective_scope, sampled:true|false}`. Use deterministic sampling by route id + user id to be stable.
leo: Security: saved views with model-scoped filters should only be visible if the viewer has access to that model in the org. Otherwise show a locked state and link to request access.
michelle: Rollout plan suggestion: feature-flag `savedviews-v2` for 10% of orgs. Start with read-only model-sourced saved views (no routing hint, no quota changes). After telemetry for confusion/regression is low, enable copy-to-route and sharing.
rollout-bot: [deploy] feature-flag `savedviews-v2` toggled for canary group: 10% orgs, region: us-west-2. Monitor: `saved_view.open`, `saved_view.copy_to_route`, error rate < 0.1%.
emily: I'll add the backend proto and a console mock with the pill and a diff modal. Will ping @michelle when done. Also adding an audit field for `applied_by` so operators can see who applied a model default to a route.
michelle: Thanks. Action items: emily backend + mock, devon telemetry events + sampling rule, leo access gating, anita backend `derived_from` pointer; jason will prototype the pill in Figma. Loop back after prototype with a short playbook for support. :thumbsup:
